blocks.text: Lots and land in Sapperton
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Character: the residential streets above East Columbia Street are single-detached homes under the RS districts of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 (2001), including some of the city's oldest housing stock around the 1891 Knox Presbyterian Church and the historic core, with secondary suites and laneway / carriage houses regulated in the same bylaw. Freehold dominates the older residential streets.

Lot sizes, as the bylaw states them: RS-1 minimum site 557.40 sq. m. / 6,000 sq. ft., FSR 0.5 (Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, s. 310). Typical Sapperton lot dimensions beyond that bylaw minimum: Not verified — no typical-size table is invented here.

ALR vs non-ALR: no Agricultural Land Reserve land is identified in Sapperton; ALR status for any specific property is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder. No ALR split is stated.

Flood position — Sapperton's own, never blended: the City's floodplain study places the industrial land along the Brunette River in Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level — the risk pocket in Sapperton is the low Brunette River / Braid-side land, not the residential slope. Lot-level status is confirmed with the City against its flood maps.

blocks.text: Development-site ground

items.t: Sapperton Green — 97 Braid Street, around Braid Station: The 38.35-acre former industrial site is designated in the OCP as the Sapperton Green Transit-Oriented Mixed-Use Community; the master plan concept endorsed by City Council (QuadReal Property Group application) proposes roughly 4,700 homes (including at least 1,122,000 sq. ft. of secured market rental and a minimum 255,000 sq. ft. of affordable housing under the City's Inclusionary Housing Policy), 750,000 to 1.5 million sq. ft. of office space, 100,000–150,000 sq. ft. of retail, a 35,000 sq. ft. community centre with child care, and 7.9 acres of publicly accessible open space, with connection to the City's Sapperton District Energy System planned. Construction timing beyond the endorsed master plan: Not verified. This is the sub-area's one true land story — and it is a plan, not a presale, not a lot offering, and counted nowhere as inventory; sellers can cite the plan, buyers should not pay today for unbuilt amenities.
The Brewery District (developer source): Wesgroup's master-planned community on the former Labatt brewery site across from Sapperton Station and the hospital carries 1.4 million sq. ft.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Sapperton

items.t: Sapperton is the historic neighbourhood at New Westminster's northeast end, on the slope above the Fraser River between McBride Boulevard and the Coquitlam boundary at Brunette Creek, taking in Royal Columbian Hospital, Sapperton and Braid SkyTrain stations, Hume Park and the Brewery District; the City also uses "McBride-Sapperton" as a neighbourhood name, and "Sapperton" is the board (GVR) sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report. Exact board boundary roads are not verified. The name is the Royal Engineers' camp nickname from 1858 — "Sappers' Town," after the Sapper rank — which stayed after the corps disbanded.
Nearby areas: Fraserview and Glenbrooke North to the west, The Heights (Victory Heights) to the north, Brunette below the hill, and Maillardville in Coquitlam across Brunette Avenue.

Transit and roads: two Expo Line stations serve the area — Sapperton Station, across from Royal Columbian Hospital, and Braid Station at the area's east end; TransLink route 109 (New Westminster Station / Lougheed Station) runs the East Columbia Street corridor. East Columbia Street, Brunette Avenue, McBride Boulevard and North Road serve the area, with Highway 1 access at the Brunette Interchange on the Coquitlam side. Driving commute times: Not verified.

Schools and catchments: SD40 catchments are address-based. A School Locator run for the sample address 331 Richmond Street (the Skwo:wech Elementary site, inside Sapperton) returned Skwo:wech Elementary (K–5), École Glenbrook Middle (6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (9–12), with Early French Immersion at École Herbert Spencer Elementary (SD40 School Locator, Baragar, run 2026-10-21) — a sample-address chain only, which does not transfer to other addresses. Skwo:wech Elementary at 331 Richmond Street officially opened June 6, 2022, replacing Richard McBride Elementary, and serves more than 400 K–5 students with an attached child care centre. School names are the Ministry-listed names.

The hospital: Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, is in Sapperton beside Sapperton Station — a regional referral hospital (cardiology, neurosurgery, high-risk obstetrics, neonatal intensive care); its Jim Pattison Acute Care Tower opened to patients on May 31, 2026 (10 storeys, 388 beds, Phase 2 of a redevelopment whose Phases 2 and 3 together are estimated at nearly $2 billion).

Parks and shopping: Hume Park and Lower Hume Park (pool, spray park, sports fields, lacrosse box, off-leash dog park) sit beside the Brunette River, the Brunette-Fraser Greenway runs through the area, Sapperton Landing Park is on the Fraser River waterfront, and Sapperton Park (1907) stands at Columbia Street and Sherbrooke Street. East Columbia Street is the commercial strip — Sapperton Plaza at East Columbia and Knox Street dates to the 1977–78 civic revitalization plan — and the Brewery District adds ground-floor retail at East Columbia and Keary Street. A grocery store in the area on an official source: Not verified. The nearest library branch is the Main Branch of the New Westminster Public Library at 716 6th Avenue in Uptown.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Sapperton

items.t: City plan: the Official Community Plan is "Our City 2041," Bylaw No. 7925 (2017), under which the Sapperton and Braid station areas are one of the City's Frequent Transit Development Areas, directing transit-supportive density around both stations, and 97 Braid Street is designated the Sapperton Green Transit-Oriented Mixed-Use Community. Sapperton Green is planned to connect to the City's Sapperton District Energy System — a City utility cost future owners there should ask about; connection for existing properties: Not confirmed.

Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 governs. Houses sit in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series, s. 310 — RS-1 minimum site 557.40 sq. m. / 6,000 sq. ft., FSR 0.5, with secondary suites and laneway / carriage houses regulated in the same bylaw), townhouse form is regulated under the older districts RT-2 through RT-2C plus RT-3/3A/3B and the newer RT-A and RT-B (at least 836.1 m² of site area, 20 m of frontage and lane access) where designated, and the hospital / Brewery District lands sit in institutional and comprehensive development districts.

Subdivision and servicing — Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 (verified): subdivision is regulated by the Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw No. 7142, 2007, which requires Approving Officer approval and ensures new lots are adequately serviced and meet the Zoning Bylaw's minimum lot size and frontage requirements, through the City's pre-application / application / Works & Services Agreement process.

Flood diligence — Zone 4, Sapperton's own position only: the Brunette River industrial land sits in Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level, while the residential slope sits above it — check the exact lot against the City's flood maps before offering on anything low near Brunette Creek or the Braid-side land. No single city-wide flood figure is stated, and no other sub-area's zone is blended in.

Heritage: Sapperton is one of the neighbourhoods documented in the City's Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements, with landmarks such as the 1891 Knox Presbyterian Church on Knox Street — confirm whether a lot's property is on the City's heritage register before planning exterior work or a teardown.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Sapperton ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

blocks.text: Good to know about Sapperton

items.t: One masterplan, two tenures, no lots. None of it is lot stock.

Sapperton Green carries a utility most buyers have never heard of. The plan connects the site to the City's Sapperton District Energy System — a future City utility cost to ask about before pricing any unit there, and a reminder that the site is a serviced-city masterplan, not raw land.

The neighbourhood's name is a rank. Sapperton is "Sappers' Town" — the 1858 Royal Engineers camp nickname outlived the corps, and Sapperton Park (1907) at Columbia and Sherbrooke was named for the Sappers; Fraser Cemetery on the hill above Columbia Street is the area's historic cemetery.

The elementary school is new, seismic-safe and named for the river. Skwo:wech Elementary (opened June 6, 2022, $34.98 million, 400+ K–5 students with an attached child care centre) replaced the seismically unsafe Richard McBride Elementary; its name is the halq'eméylem word for sturgeon, honouring Coast Salish connections to the Fraser River.

New Westminster is dense and getting denser at the stations. The 2021 Census counted 78,916 people in the city at 5,052 people per sq. km — the second-densest municipality in Canada — and the OCP directs the next density to the Sapperton and Braid station areas, which is the context for Sapperton Green's 4,700 proposed homes.
